speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: asked the Minister for Manpower of the 558 firms penalised during the recent workplace safety enforcement operations between 15 August 2022 and 17 October 2022 (a) how many firms are repeat offenders who have received penalties for workplace safety infringements previously; and (b) what is being done to prevent repeated safety breaches from happening.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The operation uncovered common contraventions such as STF hazards not identified during risk assessments, control measures not implemented for poorly maintained flooring and workers wearing inadequate footwear.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: All these contraventions required very basic mitigations for the workers’ safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: These repeat WSH offenders received stiffer penalties, such as higher composition fines compared to first time offenders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Those with poor WSH performance were also inspected more regularly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: For instance, DA Engineering Pte Ltd, a repeat WSH offender, was issued with a SWO and fined a total of $8,000 as this enforcement operation continued to uncover multiple unsafe conditions in its workplace.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The Ministry recognises that tangible improvements to unsafe WSH practices go beyond issuance of penalties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: For companies with fatal or major injuries, MOM requires them to engage external auditors to conduct a thorough review of their WSH processes and implement measures to prevent recurrence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The WSH Council has also strengthen the support for companies, especially our SMEs who need help to improve their WSH practices and processes through StartSAFE.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Under the StartSAFE programme, SMEs have access to WSH consultants who can provide professional advice and hands-on guidance on how to identify WSH risks, implement good WSH practices and prevent recurrence of a WSH offence.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Since the introduction of the Heightened Safety Period from 1 September this year, how many CEOs and Directors were made accountable for serious workplace safety breaches, what was the highest penalty imposed and if the ACOP had been used to penalise any Director thus far?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Two, as part of the Heightened Safety Period measures, how many companies had volunteered for the StartSAFE programme that the Senior Minister of State mentioned, which I believe is offered free to companies?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Are there any plans to reach out to more companies, in particular SMEs, to take up this programme?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, we are just a month into it.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Prosecutions typically take time, and therefore, I do not have an update, specific to the ACOP.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But what I can say is this: today, under section 48 of the Workplace Safety and Health Act, company directors as well as C-suite or senior leaders can already be prosecuted under the law for contraventions or not complying to workplace safety and health measures.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: ACOP helps us to put an added layer to put more transparency and clearer obligations on managements and boards so that they look after the workplace safety and health of their employees and workers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And if needed, it makes also clearer for prosecution, for us to prosecute them in Court.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But let me also give the Member some idea since he asked about what we have done so far with prosecution of board directors and senior leaders.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The director was fined $45,000 while the firm was fined $185,000.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, we do differentiate between firms and directors.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In the other case, Leeden National Oxygen Ltd was also charged under the same section 48 of the WSH Act – the ex-CEO for failure to exercise due diligence as CEO.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: He was fined $45,000 while the firm was fined $340,000.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, these are actual offences which we have prosecuted under the older regime.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But, with ACOP, it makes it easier for us to prosecute as the regime is a lot clearer.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This is close to 50% higher than what we typically got monthly before this.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But, certainly, if you ask me whether it can still be better, this is where I seek the help of the unions, for example, and employers and trade associations, to encourage more companies, because this is fully funded by the Government for SMEs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And SMEs have also been shown to have a higher incidence of fatalities and major injuries this year.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, we want to inculcate and bring more on board as much as we can.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Since the launch of ACOP as well, we have also now engaged various industry associations and companies, particularly to promote the adoption of ACOP principles and measures.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, what we will be doing next is to develop online resources on ACOP and incorporate ACOP into bizSAFE level 1 by the first quarter of 2023.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, we are going to institutionalise ACOP into our bizSAFE certification programmes and, therefore, I hope we will get more firms on board as we formalise it as well.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: We are about three months into the heightened safety period.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Can the Senior Minister of State share if this period and the measures have helped to improve the workplace safety situation across the various industries and are there any plans to extend the heightened safety period beyond 28 February 2023?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: To recap, MOM introduced a slew of measures to strengthen WSH as part of our heightened safety period from 1 September this year to 28 February next year.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, this is really to target egregious companies with serious or fatal workplace accidents.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: To date, I think we have had some promising results or outcomes so far.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I think there is greater awareness among firms.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But again, we should move towards zero because every fatality is just one too many.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, this also shows the change in posture that we are taking now, to make leaders, CEOs, a lot more accountable for fatalities and major injuries in their workplaces.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Another the heightened safety period, MOM also called for mandatory safety timeout to be completed by 30 September 2022 and we are enforcing it as we move along with inspections.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: To the Member's question whether this will be extended, the heightened safety period is still ongoing.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The initial outcomes, as I have shared, have slowed down the momentum of fatalities.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, I think that is a good sign and we hope that continues.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But it is still too early to say.
